current_episode.title: 450: The Truth About Being "That Girl" at Work

guest.titre_secondaire: Undercover Narcotics Officer and SWAT Team Member
guest.bio_context: Bridget Truxillo spent years undercover in narcotics and was the only woman on her SWAT team before leaving law enforcement to attend law school. She worked in civil litigation at a law firm for several years, then left that position to found Lady Law Shield, a law firm dedicated to representing first responders including firefighters, law enforcement officers, dispatchers, corrections officers, and EMTs. She graduated from the University of Florida with a degree in horticulture and attended the police academy the week after graduation, beginning her career with the Alachua County Sheriff's Office in Florida.

pending_qa.q: What is the relationship between small daily improvements and long-term success?
pending_qa.r: Bridget references the concept from Atomic Habits and notes that a 1% improvement every day compounds to 365% improvement over a year. She has studied the Seven Habits of Highly Effective People multiple times throughout her life and finds that concepts that seemed irrelevant in her 20s become deeply applicable by her 50s. The key is repeating these small habit-building actions consistently rather than expecting dramatic overnight transformation.

pending_qa.q: How can individuals design their day to take control of their emotional experience even when circumstances are unchangeable?
pending_qa.r: While you cannot control your supervisor, your shift schedule, or external events, you can control how you approach your day and how you feel about it. Bridget explains that feeling is a decision—nobody else has the power to make you feel something. She practices this by deciding what she wants her day to feel and look like, then taking micro-actions to support that intention, such as eating more protein to feel better physically. Even with fixed responsibilities like laundry or dealing with difficult supervisors, you can choose your attitude and design how you want to experience your day.

pending_qa.q: What legal protections and resources should women in first responder roles know about regarding reproductive health and workplace accommodations?
pending_qa.r: Women in law enforcement, firefighting, corrections, and EMS roles may face legal issues related to pumping/breastfeeding access, menstrual health accommodations, and other reproductive-related workplace needs. Bridget advises that if accommodation requests are refused verbally, follow up in writing while being delicate about wording to protect yourself. She created Lady Law Shield specifically to help first responders navigate these legal protections that many are unaware of, as even law firms may not fully understand the liabilities involved.

pending_qa.q: Why did the guest leave a well-paying law firm position to start Lady Law Shield?
pending_qa.r: Bridget left her civil litigation position at a law firm because she felt called to work that was more meaningful and aligned with her values—helping first responders facing the exact same workplace battles she experienced. She created Lady Law Shield to fill a gap she knew existed: first responders needed legal help, yes, but more importantly they needed someone to listen to them and provide answers. The firm was built around what she wished she had when she was still in law enforcement and the badge.
